script.title: Permutation vs Combination: does order matter?
script.caption_hook: Same 5 friends, same 2 picks, but 20 ways or 10 ways?

lines.say: Ma'am, same five friends, same two picks, but two different answers?
Ask one thing first. If I swap two items, is it a new result?
So if swapping gives something new, then what?
Yes means permutation: arranging, like president and secretary. No means combination: selecting, like a committee.
Okay, but how do I count them?
Take five friends, choose two for two posts. Permutation is n factorial divided by n minus r factorial.

board.title: Permutation
board.sub: n = total items, r = items taken

lines.say: Five P two is five factorial over three factorial. That's five times four, which is 20.
And combination? Order doesn't count there, right?
Right. Combination has one extra r factorial in the denominator. Same n, same r.

board.title: Combination
board.sub: n = total items, r = items chosen

lines.say: Five C two is 20 divided by two factorial, which is 2. So only 10 teams.
So the 20 counts every pair twice, once each way!
Exactly! Each chosen pair can be arranged in two ways. So nPr equals nCr times r factorial.

board.title: The link
board.sub: Select first, then arrange r items

lines.say: So P for position, C for committee!
Remember: if order matters, permutation. If order doesn't matter, combination.
